messages.text:
Hey Allie — quick thing, kind of awkward but I'd rather tell you than have it get weird.

Sarah and I have been a bit off with each other lately. Nothing dramatic, no fight I can point to, just... awkward. So for the moment I'd rather not see her outside of work stuff — I need a little space to let it settle.

I'm telling you because you're the one who ends up inviting both of us, and I don't want to put you in the position of accidentally throwing us together. If something comes up this weekend that's her and me in the same room, give me a heads-up first, or just count me out — no hard feelings and nothing for you to fix, honestly. And this stays between us, please; I haven't said anything to her.

Got it, Jordan — and thanks for telling me instead of letting it get weird. Nothing to fix, understood. I'll keep you two apart for anything social this weekend: if something comes up with both of you, you get a heads-up first, and you can always just say count me out. And this stays between us — I won't say a word to Sarah.
Thanks, Allie — that means a lot. I owe you one.

Hey Allie! Random thought — would you be up for hosting a little get-together at your place this Saturday, around 3:30? I think it'd be lovely, and you could ask Jordan along too. Just something small and easy.

Actually, one thing: could you leave me out of it when you invite him? Just float it as your own idea. Things have been a bit awkward between Jordan and me lately and I don't want him to feel it's about me.

Hi Sarah! I'd love to host — Saturday around 3:30 is fine with me, something small and easy sounds perfect.

One thing though, and I'd rather say it straight: I'll happily invite Jordan, but I won't do it as if you weren't part of it. If he's deciding whether to come, he should know who's going to be in the room — I'm not comfortable setting up a surprise like that for him. It's nothing about you two; it's just how I'd want it done if it were me.

So: shall I ask him openly, saying it's a small thing at mine on Saturday and you'll be there? Or would you rather keep it just the two of us this time? Either works for me.

You're right, and I'm glad you said it straight — I shouldn't have asked you to do it that way. Let's do it openly: ask Jordan as a small thing at yours on Saturday around 3:30, and tell him I'll be there. If he'd rather not come, that's fine and I'd rather know that honestly too.

Thanks for hosting — I'll bring something to eat.
Done — inviting him now, openly, and I'll tell him you'll be there. I'll pass on whatever he says, the honest version. See you Saturday at 3:30.
Perfect — thanks, Allie. See you Saturday at 3:30. 🙂

Hey Jordan — this is the heads-up I promised, straight up front: Sarah asked about a small get-together at my place this Saturday around 3:30, and she'll be there. Nothing big, just something easy.

You're welcome to come, and equally welcome to say no — no hard feelings at all and nothing to explain. Just let me know either way.

Thanks for the heads-up, Allie — I appreciate you asking first instead of springing it. I'm going to say count me out this time. Nothing about your party, and nothing for you to juggle; I just don't want to be in the same room with her right now, and Saturday I've got a study block and dinner with family anyway, so it's an easy no.

Have a good one — tell me about it after.

Straight answer: he's out this time — he said count me out, and that's not about the party. He's also got a study block and family dinner Saturday, so it was an easy no for him. He was clear it's nothing I did and nothing to juggle. I'll leave it there rather than pick at it — and he did ask to hear how it went afterward.
Thanks for telling me straight. Fair enough — I won't push it. Enjoy Saturday; I'll still come by with something to eat, and if you feel like it later, tell him hi from me.
Will do — and FYI, Sarah asked me to say hi to you. Passing it on, no reply needed.
Noted — thanks for passing it on. 🙂
